meta.title: Datasets
meta.description: The world of transport services as our datasets document it: intermodal rail, Baltic shortsea, refrigerated carriers in Germany, Rhine barge — as an animation, not a search tool.

hero.title: Transport services, seen from above.
hero.lede: Intermodal, shortsea, refrigerated, barge: our datasets document geolocated sites and the services that link them. We show them as an animation — not as a directory to search.

world.title: Four field stories, one turning globe.
world.lede: The globe plays four chapters: intermodal rail in Europe, shortsea in the Baltic, refrigerated carriers in Germany, barge on the Rhine. Nothing to type, nothing to query: you watch, pause, or move on to the next chapter.

items.name: Referenced is not available.
items.body: A site or service shown here is referenced: that does not mean capacity is free on your corridor. Availability is confirmed by a written answer.

items.name: Sites, not exact routes.
items.body: Sites are placed to within about a kilometre; links are arcs joining a start to an end, not the actual path of a train, ship or truck. No vehicle is tracked.

items.name: What is named is published.
items.body: When an operator name appears, it has been cleared for publication. Without clearance, the link appears without a name: we do not fill in the blanks.

protection.title: A static showcase; a database that stays private.
protection.lede: Anything a public site displays can be copied: we do not pretend to prevent it. So we settle the question upstream — the source database is never online, and the site only publishes what we are comfortable seeing copied.

tiers.name: Private database
tiers.body: Sources, contacts, qualifications, precise coordinates. Maintained by an administrator, outside this site: it has neither access nor credentials.

tiers.name: Validated export
tiers.body: One publication at a time, triggered by a person. Allowed columns only, capped volume, coordinates rounded to about 1 km, names checked. The difference from the previous version is reviewed before release.

tiers.name: Static showcase
tiers.body: A single file, built into the site when it is built. No API, no request to the database, nothing to query: what is published is what is shown.

protection.limit: Stated limit: the showcase can be copied in full. It contains only what we are comfortable seeing copied — no volumes, no prices, no precise coordinates.

coverage.title: What the showcase contains — and nothing else.
coverage.lede: The format is closed: data that is not provided for is not published — it makes the publication fail.

rows.name: Sites
rows.content: Name, type (port, rail-road terminal, inland port, hub, carrier base), country.

rows.name: Links
rows.content: Mode, start site, up to three intermediate sites, end site, chapter.
rows.grain: An arc between sites, not the actual path.

rows.name: Operator
rows.content: A name, only if it has been cleared for publication.

rows.name: Volume
rows.content: At most 250 sites and 400 links, 80 per chapter.
rows.grain: Capped at publication and when the site is built.

coverage.legendNote: Any other column in an export — a price, a contact, an internal identifier — blocks the publication instead of being quietly dropped.

cta.title: Need the detail?
cta.body: What we know about a specific corridor is shared as part of a discussion about your scope.

demo.note: Demonstration links between real sites. No operator is named and none of these links is asserted.

flat.nowebgl: Your browser does not display 3D: here is the flat map, with the same links.
flat.software: Your device has no 3D acceleration: here is the flat map, with the same links.
flat.lightweight: To spare your connection and your device, the map is flat: same links, no 3D.
flat.lost: The 3D display was interrupted: here is the flat map, with the same links.

rail-intermodal.name: Intermodal rail in Europe
rail-intermodal.body: Rail-road terminals and North Sea ports, linked by the main axes: Rhine–Alpine, central Europe, the Mediterranean.

baltic-shortsea.name: Shortsea in the Baltic
baltic-shortsea.body: Short sea links between German, Polish, Baltic, Swedish and Finnish ports: the sea as one link in a transport chain.

reefer-germany.name: Refrigerated carriers in Germany
reefer-germany.body: Carriers specialised in temperature-controlled transport, spread across Germany, and the destinations they serve.

barge-rhine.name: Barge on the Rhine
barge-rhine.body: Inland ports linked by barge, from the North Sea ports up to the Upper Rhine.

list.summary: See all the links as a list
list.intro: Text equivalent of the animation: every link, chapter by chapter.
